title: Do you look better than Silver Era lifters？ (Physique Review LIVE)
summary: Three-hour live stream (his third) where NH, while sick, reviews about 20 viewer physiques, including the first woman submitted, naming each person's strong and weak points and what to prioritise. Between reviews he answers chat questions on evolving rep ranges, rep range choice, bulking size, giant sets, abs and obliques, natural status and his own lifts.
claims: At the most basic level weight loss is calories in versus calories out; saying otherwise gives overweight people an excuse, and macro or micronutrient peculiarities matter only in rare cases
You stop being a novice when linear progression with few exercises and little volume stops working and you need new exercises, more days, more frequency and more volume
Strength standards say nothing about whether you are intermediate: some people bench 225 lb two weeks in and others take two years, which only reflects strength genetics
He knew a lifter with a near 4-plate bench, 5-plate squat and 6-plate deadlift who was still a novice: novice program, novice understanding, novice work capacity, just gifted for strength
Every one of his programs uses evolving rep ranges, and most modern programs do the same without naming it
Evolving rep range: give each lift a range such as 6-10, pick a weight that keeps you in it, add reps week to week (6-7 then 7-8), and once you hit the top add weight but keep the same range
Only one set has to reach the top of the rep range before you add weight; never change the rep range itself or the system breaks
After 15 years of training he still gets several rep PRs almost every session, and rep PRs add up to weight PRs over time
Dips and bench press are about equal for hypertrophy; dips are a better overall builder of triceps and shoulders if your shoulders tolerate them

Fat grips ruin hammer curls by turning a brachialis movement into grip work; they suit pull-ups, supinated curls, and triceps work like V-bar extensions or skull crushers, where they ease wrists and elbows
Since age 14 he has never gone more than a week without training; he must be physically active every day for his mental health, so rest days become weighted-carry days
He reads 12-15 hours a week, rereads a book at least five times before presenting it, and takes notes and writes essays on one of those reads
Wrist pain from pressing overuse: change exercise variations, add high-rep wrist curls, and use a rice bucket

His priority muscles are shoulders, triceps, forearms and calves; quads grow fast on 3-6 sets a week while shoulders on 14-15 weekly sets cannot keep pace, because strong points stay strong and weak points stay weak
He ego-lifted reverse curls up to 100 lb with sloppy form, then dropped to about 70 lb with proper form
He likes shoulders that look small next to the upper arm, but shoulders still have to grow as the arm grows

Lateral delt isolation before or after pressing makes little difference, and doing it before dips makes dips feel better; never isolate triceps before dips or presses because they become the limiting factor
He eats much less protein than usually recommended, about 100-120 g a day
People who send physiques often misjudge their own strong and weak points
Many lifters he reviews are back dominant, possibly from the advice to pull twice as much as you push; they need less back volume and more front-of-body volume
Lean young lifters who started out chubby must not fear bulking; maintaining would be a mistake when they need a surplus to keep growing
Look into imbalances such as uneven shoulder blades while young; the longer you wait the more they set in
Start isolating the neck as early as possible; it ties the physique together
The most muscular pose frames the abs with the arms, so without a six-pack there is nothing in the middle to show
One reviewer trained back once a week against nearly three press days and was still back dominant: some people are simply gifted for back
Enhanced physiques tend to be developed everywhere, especially delts and traps; clearly lagging areas count as evidence a lifter may be natural
You need several exercises per muscle: incline curls alone will stall around 35-45 lb dumbbells for 12 because one stimulus cannot break the plateau
Novices need 1-2 exercises per muscle and more later, but never more than 4-5; small variations are unlimited
Rear delt work is good for bodybuilding and for shoulder health, and dips paradoxically help shoulders too
If you are overweight, lift while you cut; it makes the cut easier and you look better at the end
Someone who lost a lot of weight but is still soft should recomp at maintenance for about a year and a half before adding a surplus, because waist fat comes back first
Telling novices to just grow everything is bad advice: everyone has dormant strong and weak points, and catching them early prevents years of playing catch-up
He wishes someone had told him one year in that his biceps were far ahead of his triceps; now he plays catch-up
Most people only discover what physique or sport they want after lifting for a while
Pick a rep range from preference and the nature of the lift: compounds lower, isolation higher; rear delt work at 3-5 reps or weighted dips at 10-15 are mismatched
All his work is 3-15 reps, mostly 6-12; he goes higher only on some forearm and neck exercises, and above 20 reps he considers junk volume
You can bulk indefinitely only if you do it properly; otherwise you cycle getting fat and cutting like a hamster on a wheel
He bulks on the bare minimum surplus that still makes him gain weight
Long arms make biceps and forearms harder to develop; long-limbed lifters are favoured on pulls but disadvantaged on curls, and his short humerus makes curling easier
With a short biceps insertion and big forearms, emphasise supinated curls with the pinky twisted outward
Back thickness comes from work for erectors and rhomboids plus heavy movements: heavy RDLs, heavy dumbbell rows, barbell rows, heavy power shrugs
To break a pull-up plateau, add a variation with a different grip
Michael Gundill is one of the best sources of bodybuilding information
In an old photo he weighed 10 lb less than now yet looked much fatter, which shows how much body composition matters
Full body is very flexible; to prioritise arms, just put a lot of arm isolation into it
For abs, two sets every time you train is a good way to overload
Best oblique movements: side twists, side twists on a hyperextension bench, suitcase deadlifts
If bench does not hit your chest, swap it for weighted push-ups and weighted dips, and add chest isolation on another day
Training obliques does not widen the waist; love handles are fat, not muscle, and the only exception he saw was on steroids
His forearms are long relative to his humerus, so he puts high priority on forearm training to make them look massive
A small posterior chain with a tight waist is the classic silver-era look; Steve Reeves' ideal was neck, arms and calves the same size
A 19-year-old going from 130 to 180 lb in three years is a lot of muscle and shows bodybuilding genetics; he could reach 190-195 lb
If 12 weekly sets for arms are not making them grow, check whether you progress; if not, change exercises or revisit volume, possibly lowering it
Stacking plates on the forehead for neck curls lets the arms help; he uses a head harness with the weight hanging behind him on a preacher bench through full range, which is much harder
Not everyone can reach a 4-plate bench since it depends on being built for it and staying uninjured, but he believes everyone can reach a 4-plate dip
His best bench is 335 lb; 350 seems possible but 405 is out of reach without drugs, whereas a 5-7 plate dip feels achievable because he can train dips without getting hurt
Banded curls are excellent: good resistance curve, safe, and allow rest-pause; it is the only curl he really feels in his biceps
Banded curls: band looped deep in the hand to supinate, a tension he can do only 6-7 reps with, 15 s rest-pause for more reps, target 8-12, progress when he reaches 12
He dropped bench press because flat-back benching for full range destroyed his shoulders
Even stage-ready physiques always have at least two areas to improve
To replace RDLs and deadlifts, use hyperextensions, glute-ham raises and good mornings
With narrow clavicles, prioritise arms and get as much shoulder size as possible to create the illusion of size
He does not compete because he will not lose weight; like Rich Piana he wants to be too big for doors, looks worse shredded, and lacks the motivation; good tested natural federations do exist now

At his gym one IFBB pro trains very heavy and another never lifts over 30 lb with 50-rep giant sets, yet they look equally good: drug response matters more than training for them, which is impossible for naturals
Be skeptical of training advice from most enhanced pros; some coast on an exceptional drug response

For front lats do weighted chin-ups with a grip slightly narrower than shoulders, once a week only, without fully extending at the bottom to protect the biceps; the other session use supinated lat pulldowns or dumbbell pullovers
Coming back from a long break: two 45-minute sessions a week, favourite exercises, minimal volume of about two sets
Starting every workout with calves sounds like the fix until you realise it is boring, which is why people skip calves
Past the novice stage, evolving rep ranges are the main progression method; tempo is a way to standardise reps, not something to progress
Chin-ups feel like more front lat for him; wide pull-ups bring in a lot of traps
He avoids behind-the-neck work; any press meant for delts has to be in the scapular plane with elbows slightly forward or his shoulders hurt
He does not time rest; he knows roughly what 3 minutes feels like or uses a song or a bit of podcast
He is not a fan of straight-arm pulldowns, and hybrid movements like the Bradford press are not worth it
Do dumbbell pullovers without scapular retraction

He used giant sets from his first day to save time; build up gradually: easy supersets (biceps+triceps), easy giant sets (biceps+triceps+rear delts), hard supersets (press+pull), then hard giant sets (press+pull+abs)
Lifting during a deficit preserves more muscle than dieting without training
Free volume that is easy to superset: reverse pec deck, leg curls, wrist curls, calf raises, which add volume without systemic fatigue
A lower-body compound paired with anything in a superset wrecks the cardio system; doing the whole workout as one giant set sabotages performance
After a long deficit, move toward muscle gain by raising volume from the novice program with more hip hinges and extensions
His favourite shoulder movements: Smith overhead press on a near-vertical bench, shallow incline press, cable lateral raises; upright rows are a valid shoulder isolation that was wrongly demonised
An imbalance is fine if it is on purpose, like his arms over shoulders; most are accidents, and bodybuilding should not have accidents
For a lifter with dominant delts and lagging limbs, a dedicated limb-focus program would make sense
For a 6'3 lifter who gained 40 lb in 1.5 years: a 4-day split with two arm-focused days (one triceps, one biceps and forearms)
Kettlebell training is inferior for hypertrophy and okay only as minimalist training
Trap isolation is not necessary since back compounds train traps, though trap-biased compounds can help
Training on an empty stomach is mostly stupid; you want energy, just not a full stomach
A pinched nerve can cause atrophy and loss of function; treat it before thinking about gains
Getting big from calisthenics alone is very hard; mix free weights with calisthenics
Upper traps: Kelso shrugs, cheat or power shrugs, upright rows, lateral raises for trap-sensitive people, heavy Kroc rows with semi-flared elbows that stretch the traps
A bulk that gains 40 lb is too much; the surplus only needs to support building muscle, so halve it, gain half the fat and stay reasonably lean
Your first bulk is like a first love that cannot be repeated; each later bulk should be more conservative, while lifters do the opposite and only force fat
A 300 kcal surplus is plenty; going up to 500 is pointless
Former athletes (football, wrestling) have a better base than people who start straight with bodybuilding, and a great back often reflects years of heavy lifting
One ab and one oblique movement at three sets each, six weekly sets, is okay
Train abs 3-4 times a week if possible; try cable crunches, knee raises and the underrated ab crunch machine
Russian twists are hit or miss; side twists and oblique raises on a hyperextension bench let you play with range of motion
Knee raises are much easier to progressively overload than leg raises
Bigger obliques make love handles look smaller and tighten the whole side of the core, since obliques run along the core and not from the hips
Bust a vertical press plateau with drop sets: do as many sets as you can within the rep range at working weight, then lower the weight for an extra set
Smith machine split squats are a better option than the free-weight version
There are no natural steroids: if it works it is a steroid; tongkat-type supplements do not work and those who say they do sell them
Creatine is natural, cheap and works, but the effect is small
Visible-but-flat abs come from building them with weighted crunches, cable crunches and weighted sit-ups, not from cutting
Women tend to have great biceps genetics, with delts slightly smaller than the upper arm
Quad-dominant lifters should emphasise hip hinges to balance development and protect the knees
Powerlifting builds a dominant lower body and a thick back without the detail bodybuilders want
Training 3x a week with weak chest and shoulders: make two of them push days, one horizontal and one vertical
A simple chest and triceps day: one horizontal press, one long-head triceps isolation, one lateral-head triceps isolation, one chest isolation
Natural lifters can earn an IFBB pro card but will not win the biggest shows
Nucleus overload works for abs with cable or machine crunches; avoid movements that tax the hips
Abs can be trained and improve during a cut; weak areas can come up without a big surplus
exercises: more chest, lats do not rub the arms
fat grips turn it into a grip exercise
Fat-grip pull-ups, supinated curls, V-bar extensions, skull crushers
more comfortable on wrists and elbows
help wrist pain from pressing overuse
stalls if it is the only biceps movement
grip slightly narrower than shoulders; do not fully extend at the bottom; once a week
chest substitute when bench does not hit chest
loop deep in the hand to supinate; 6-7 rep tension, 15 s rest-pause, 8-12
on preacher bench, weight hanging behind, full ROM
plates on the forehead let the arms help
valid shoulder and trap isolation, wrongly demonised
hurts his shoulders; press in the scapular plane
hybrid movements are not worth it
Heavy RDL, barbell row, heavy dumbbell row, power shrugs
semi-open elbow, let the weight stretch the traps
Cable crunch, knee raise, ab crunch machine
Squats and split squats with feet facing forward
Reverse pec deck, leg curls, wrist curls, calf raises
viewer_questions: is weight loss just calories in calories out
when to move from novice to intermediate volume
why progress lifts and use multiple biceps exercises
do pro bodybuilders know how to train
